description:
At EY, we’re all in to shape your future with confidence.

We’ll help you succeed in a globally connected powerhouse of diverse teams and take your career wherever you want it to go.

Join EY and help to build a better working world.

The opportunity

Transfer pricing sits at the intersection of tax, economics and business strategy. As a Tax Staff in our Transfer Pricing practice, you will help multinational organizations analyze how value is created across their operations and translate that analysis into clear, well-supported transfer pricing positions. Working with economists and tax professionals across Canada and EY’s global network, you will contribute to documentation, planning, audit defence and process improvement projects while building a strong foundation in transfer pricing consulting.

This job posting relates to an existing vacancy within our organization.

Your key responsibilities

  • Analyze financial, operational and industry information to support transfer pricing engagements.
  • Conduct company, industry and comparable transaction research using relevant databases and public information.
  • Assist with transfer pricing documentation, planning analyses, advance pricing arrangements and audit defence materials.
  • Apply economic, finance and accounting concepts to understand client facts and develop practical, evidence-based conclusions.
  • Prepare clear work products, calculations and presentations that communicate findings to team members and clients.
  • Collaborate with colleagues across tax, economics and other disciplines to deliver coordinated client work.
  • Manage assigned work against project timelines, raise questions early and contribute to team priorities.
  • Use data and technology tools to improve the efficiency, consistency and quality of analyses and deliverables.

Skills and attributes for success

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with close attention to detail and an interest in understanding how businesses operate.
  • The ability to organize multiple priorities, meet deadlines and adapt as project needs change.
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain analysis in a concise and practical way.
  • A collaborative approach and the confidence to ask questions, share ideas and take ownership of assigned work.
  • Working knowledge of Microsoft Excel, Word and PowerPoint.

Qualifications

  • An undergraduate degree in economics, accounting, finance, business, mathematics, data analytics or a related field.

Ideally, you’ll also have

  • Coursework, internship or work experience related to tax, economics, accounting, finance, consulting or data analysis.
  • Exposure to financial statements, economic research, business valuation or statistical analysis.
  • An interest in transfer pricing, international tax and the commercial decisions of multinational organizations.
  • Experience using data visualization, automation or AI-enabled tools responsibly to support research and analysis.

We’re looking for curious, analytical people who enjoy working through complex information and turning it into clear conclusions. You’ll bring sound judgment, attention to detail and a collaborative mindset, along with the motivation to keep learning as tax rules, business models and technology evolve. This role is well suited to someone who wants to build technical depth while gaining broad exposure to how multinational organizations operate.

title: Senior adviseur Noordzee
description:
Dit ga je doen

De Noordzee is het grootste natuurgebied van Nederland en het epicentrum van de energietransitie. Als senior adviseur bij Rijkswaterstaat werk je mee aan het vernieuwde Programma Noordzee en verbind je nationale en internationale belangen. Zoek jij een rol waarin jouw bestuurlijke advisering direct merkbaar is op de Noordzee? Bekijk hieronder wat deze taak inhoudt.

Hoe jij bijdraagt

Bij de herziening van het Programma Noordzee 2022-2027 speel je een centrale rol in de ruimtelijke ordening op zee. Je vindt de juiste balans tussen duurzame energieproductie, de beheertaken van Rijkswaterstaat en andere belangrijke gebruiksfuncties. Zo borg je bijvoorbeeld dat zandwinning voor kustlijnzorg voldoende ruimte krijgt, in evenwicht met de ecologie op zee. In een internationale omgeving stem je af met buurlanden over grensoverschrijdende effecten.

Jouw werkzaamheden

  • Je vertaalt belangen van Rijkswaterstaat naar strategische beleidsvoorstellen.
  • Je ondersteunt de uitvoering bij de implementatie van beleid.
  • Je organiseert de balans tussen zandwinning voor de kust en ruimte voor de natuur.
  • Je weegt belangen af tussen de verschillende drukfactoren op de Noordzee om tot goede ruimtelijke ordening te komen.
  • Je stemt Noordzee beheer af in overleg met internationale partners en buurlanden.

Jouw team

Vanuit Rijswijk werk je samen met een betrokken team van deskundigen en uitvoering aan de grote uitdagingen op de Noordzee. De collega's verbinden beleid direct met de dagelijkse praktijk van het mariene beheer. Binnen de afdeling deel je kennis en werk je nauw samen met interne en externe partners. Zo pak je complexe dossiers gezamenlijk en effectief op.

Interesse?

Solliciteren is zo geregeld. In plaats van een standaard brief vragen we je om je cv te uploaden en in het sollicitatieformulier kort antwoord te geven op de vragen hieronder (maximaal 200 woorden per vraag):
  1. Motivatie: wat spreekt jou aan in deze functie en de rol van Rijkswaterstaat op de Noordzee?
  2. Omgevingsbewustzijn: beschrijf een situatie waarin internationale of interdepartementale belangen invloed hadden op jouw advisering.
  3. Oordeelsvorming: kun je een situatie beschrijven waarin je op basis van complexe en onvolledige informatie een zwaarwegend advies moest uitbrengen?
We raden je aan om bij de situatievragen een concreet voorbeeld te gebruiken. Het kan je helpen die vragen te beantwoorden volgens de STARR-methode (Situatie, Taak, Actie, Resultaat, Reflectie).

Meer weten?

Hier kom je te werken

Over Rijkswaterstaat

Rijkswaterstaat

Rijkswaterstaat is de uitvoeringsorganisatie van het ministerie van Infrastructuur en Waterstaat en bestaat uit 6 landelijke en 7 regionale organisatieonderdelen. Al meer dan 225 jaar werken we dagelijks aan een veilig, leefbaar en bereikbaar Nederland. We beheren en ontwikkelen de rijkswegen, -vaarwegen en -wateren en zetten in op een duurzame leefomgeving. Samen met anderen werken we aan een land dat beschermd is tegen overstromingen. Waar voldoende groen is, en voldoende en schoon water. En waar je vlot en veilig van A naar B kunt. Samenwerken aan een veilig, leefbaar en bereikbaar Nederland: dat is werken bij Rijkswaterstaat.

Talent als basis, diversiteit als kracht

Rijkswaterstaat is een inclusieve organisatie. Een organisatie die ruimte biedt aan iedereen en die de kracht van de diversiteit van medewerkers gebruikt om samen betere resultaten te halen voor Nederland. Inclusief betekent dat iedereen zich betrokken en gewaardeerd voelt; niet ondanks, maar dankzij de verschillen. Daarom nodigen wij jou graag uit, als jij je herkent in deze vacature, om te solliciteren.

Rijkswaterstaat Zee en Delta

Wil jij werken bij Rijkswaterstaat binnen Zee en Delta (ZD)? Dit organisatieonderdeel beheert de Deltawateren, de Noordzee en het zeegebied in Caribisch Nederland. Ook maakt zij het vervoer over die zeegebieden en het Zeeuwse land en water mogelijk. Samen met onder andere kustgemeenten en waterschappen verzorgt ZD het kustbeheer van Nederland en wordt de toegang tot de belangrijke havens van Rotterdam, Amsterdam en Antwerpen geborgd. Internationaal gezien is ZD dé gesprekspartner en kennisspecialist op het gebied van de drukst bevaren zee ter wereld.

Werken aan een duurzame leefomgeving is waar ZD voor staat. Dat vraagt om een intensieve en goede samenwerking. Belangrijke partners zijn de Haagse beleidsdepartementen. Samen met hen werkt ZD proactief aan de ontwikkeling van gezamenlijke netwerken.

Voor de toekomst zet ZD in op windenergie, energiebesparing en -opwekking, onderhoud in de Zuidwestelijke Delta, de doorontwikkeling van de Deltawerken en het uitvoeringsprogramma Caribisch Nederland. Dat laatste wordt onder meer gedaan met wegonderhoud, milieuprojecten en verbetering van haveninfrastructuur.

Afdeling Netwerkontwikkeling en Visie

De afdeling Netwerkontwikkeling en Visie (NOV) zorgt voor een heldere regionale uitwerking van de netwerkbeheervisie van Rijkswaterstaat en houdt daarbij rekening met ontwikkelingen en de partners in de regio.

De afdeling levert integrale en gebiedsgerichte adviezen over water, mobiliteit, ruimte en duurzaamheid. We volgen de actuele ontwikkelingen binnen de regio en op het gebied van wetgeving en beleid. Op basis van onze kennis adviseren we de directie over onder meer bestuurlijke en strategische lange termijn vraagstukken. Daarnaast vertalen we actuele ontwikkelingen naar visies en strategieën voor ons organisatieonderdeel en de landelijke netwerkbeheervisie van Rijkswaterstaat. Ook dragen we bij aan de omgevingsvisies van onze partners in de regio. Om dit goed te kunnen doen, maken we gebruik van een breed netwerk binnen Rijkswaterstaat, het ministerie van Infrastructuur en Waterstaat, regionale overheden en andere partners.

Bijzonderheden

  • Bij voldoende geschikte reacties kan de vacature eerder sluiten.
  • Reizen voor internationaal overleg maakt onderdeel uit van de functie.
  • Om bij ons te werken, moet je een Verklaring Omtrent Gedrag (VOG) kunnen overhandigen, ook als je een interdepartementale transfer maakt. De kosten voor het aanvragen van een VOG worden door ons vergoed.
  • Je wordt ingeschaald op basis van ervaring.
  • Het inwinnen van referenties kan deel uitmaken van het sollicitatieproces, dit doen we altijd in overleg met jou.
  • Het maken van een casus en (online) screening via onder meer databanken kan deel uitmaken van het sollicitatieproces.

title: Senior Software Engineer — Service Observability & Detection
description:
Imagine what you could do here. At Apple, new ideas have a way of becoming extraordinary products, services, and customer experiences very quickly. Apple Pay and Wallet are at the heart of how millions of people around the world make payments, store credentials, and interact with commerce every day. Behind every tap, every transaction, and every boarding pass is a set of systems that must be fast, reliable, and secure at massive scale. We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer to join the Service Observability & Detection team within Wallet, Payments, and Commerce (WPC). In this role, you will design and build the telemetry foundations, SLO frameworks, and detection systems that give engineering and operations teams deep, real-time visibility into the health of services that hundreds of millions of people depend on every day. You will define what "good" looks like for telemetry at scale — and build systems that ensure we detect failures before our customers do.

Apple Pay processes billions of transactions across millions of merchants worldwide. The systems behind Apple Pay, Apple Wallet, Apple Cash, Tap to Pay, and our commerce platforms must meet the highest standards for availability, latency, security, and correctness — with zero tolerance for downtime or data loss.

Our team owns the observability and detection layer across all WPC services. We don't just consume telemetry — we define the telemetry strategy, build the instrumentation standards, and design the SLO and alerting architectures that turn raw signals into actionable detection. We work at the intersection of platform engineering, reliability, and operations — building systems that scale across hundreds of services, thousands of APIs, and billions of transactions.

This is a senior engineering role within one of Apple's most critical and high-scale service organizations. You will work cross-functionally with multiple product and engineering teams — partnering directly with offering owners, platform teams, and operations — to build observability and detection systems that the entire organization depends on. You will lead by influence, drive adoption across teams you don't manage, and set the telemetry and reliability standards that shape how WPC builds, monitors, and operates services at scale.

Minimum Qualifications

  • 8+ years of experience in software engineering with deep expertise in observability, reliability engineering, or telemetry platform development.
  • Proven track record of leading cross-functional technical initiatives — driving alignment, adoption, and delivery across multiple engineering teams you don't directly manage.
  • Experience building telemetry and observability systems from the ground up — not just configuring tools, but designing instrumentation strategies, telemetry pipelines, and data models that scale to thousands of services and billions of events.
  • Deep hands-on experience with OpenTelemetry — SDK instrumentation, Collector architecture (agent and gateway tiers), processors, exporters, context propagation, and metadata enrichment at scale.
  • Strong understanding of SLOs, SLIs, and error budgets — with hands-on experience defining, implementing, and operating SLO-based alerting in production.
  • Experience designing alerting architectures for complex distributed systems — including burn-rate alerts, multi-signal correlation, intelligent routing, and alert storm prevention.
  • Strong proficiency in at least two of: Kotlin, Java, Go, or Python.
  • Experience with observability platforms such as Datadog, Grafana, Prometheus, or Splunk — including APM, metrics, traces, monitors, and dashboards.
  • Deep understanding of distributed systems concepts including microservices architectures, API gateways, event-driven systems, and service-to-service dependencies.
  • Experience solving hard telemetry problems at scale — sampling strategies, high-cardinality metric management, tail-based sampling, cross-service trace stitching, and pipeline reliability under load.
  • Strong communication and stakeholder management skills — ability to translate complex technical observability concepts into clear strategies for engineering leadership and partner teams.
  • Demonstrated ability to establish org-wide engineering standards and drive adoption through influence, documentation, and tooling rather than mandate.
  • BS or MS in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience working on payment systems, financial services platforms, or other high-compliance, high-availability domains.
  • Experience building observability platforms or telemetry infrastructure that serves an entire engineering organization — not just a single team.
  • Experience leading technical initiatives across organizational boundaries — building consensus, defining standards, and driving adoption without direct authority.
  • Experience applying AI/ML to operational problems such as anomaly detection, intelligent alert grouping, automated incident correlation, or predictive alerting.
  • Familiarity with incident management workflows and tools — understanding how detection feeds into triage, escalation, and resolution.
  • Experience with Infrastructure-as-Code tools such as Terraform or Pulumi for managing observability resources (monitors, SLOs, dashboards) as code.
  • Experience with service catalog or service registry systems — ownership models, dependency mapping, and health scoring at organizational scale.
  • Experience building systems that serve both engineering teams and SOC/NOC operators — balancing depth of signal with clarity of action.

title: Early Career Substation Engineer
description:
WSP is currently initiating a search for an Entry Level Substation Engineer for our Syracuse, New York office.

Be involved in projects with our Substation Team and be a part of a growing organization that meets our clients’ objectives and solves their challenges.

This Opportunity

As demand for electricity continues to surge, the power industry is undergoing one of the largest infrastructure expansions in decades. Utilities, data center developers, manufacturers, and renewable energy providers are investing billions to modernize and expand the electric grid. In this role, you'll help design the substations and electrical infrastructure that make this growth possible while working alongside experienced engineers on projects that power communities, support emerging technologies, and shape the future of energy. From day one, you'll gain hands-on experience, meaningful responsibilities, and exposure to projects that have a lasting impact on how electricity is delivered across North America.

If you're energized by large-scale infrastructure projects, enjoy solving complex technical challenges, and want to help shape the future of digital infrastructure, this is an opportunity to make a lasting impact while accelerating your career on some of the most significant power delivery projects being developed today.

In this role, you’ll help shape the early vision for substation design and electrical infrastructure supporting cutting-edge projects. You’ll contribute to developing preliminary concepts and layouts that inform key feasibility and planning decisions—giving you exposure to the most strategic phase of project delivery. This role contributes to early-stage substation planning and design development for clients, working collaboratively across business lines to support feasibility, site evaluation, and infrastructure planning.

WSP brings global expertise in power delivery, power generation, and program management—anchored by the acquisition of POWER Engineers, Inc. TRC Companies have now joined WSP, deepening our power practice and expanding our energy advisory and intelligent grid services. We're partnering with clients to shape how energy systems evolve around the world—and we need your help.

Your Impact

  • Support multidisciplinary coordination for site evaluation, planning, and infrastructure integration.
  • Contribute to proposal development, including technical input and scope definition.
  • Assist in execution of substation projects across planning, design, procurement, and construction phases.
  • Coordinate with internal teams, utilities, vendors, and stakeholders for project delivery.
  • Participate in site visits and field activities to validate design assumptions and resolve issues.
  • Support development of project schedules, deliverables, and budgets.
  • Perform substation design tasks including:
    • One-line diagrams, schematics, and wiring diagrams.
    • Layouts, grounding, lightning protection, and basic SCADA systems.
  • Prepare design deliverables such as general arrangements, sections, BOMs, and cable/conduit plans.
  • Support development of equipment specifications and vendor coordination.
  • Follow QA/QC procedures and verify accuracy of deliverables.
  • Prepare reports, calculations, and technical documentation.
  • Work collaboratively with senior engineers and project leads.
  • Maintain compliance with codes, standards, and company policies.
  • Exercise responsible and ethical decision-making regarding company funds, resources, and conduct, and adhere to WSP’s Code of Conduct and related policies and procedures.
  • Perform additional responsibilities as required by business needs.

title: Sr Hydrocarbon Scheduler
description:
CITGO PETROLEUM CORPORATION

CITGO Petroleum Corporation is a recognized leader in the refining industry and operates under the well-known CITGO brand. CITGO owns and operates three refineries located in Lake Charles, LA.; Lemont, IL.; and Corpus Christi, TX, and wholly and/or jointly owns 43 active terminals, nine pipelines and three lubricants blending and packaging plants. With approximately 3,300 employees and a combined crude capacity of approximately 829,000 barrels-per-day (bpd), positions CITGO as one of the best-branded supplier companies in the industry.

At CITGO our people are our most important resource. Our core values are Safety, Integrity, Respect, Accountability, and Care.

Job Summary

This position is a ladder progression in the job classification of Hydrocarbon Scheduler. It reflects an accomplished career in multiple-hydrocarbon scheduling at a corporate or functional level. The experience gathered by the incumbent may include as well exposure to the areas of Marine Operations, Vessel or Barge Operations Coordination, Rail and Freight, etc. at both domestic and international llevels The experience and demonstrated performance on scheduling activities shall make the incumbent key provider of scheduling advice to the commercial and supply teams typically on specific hydrocarbons or geographies, new IT solutions or upgrades, and on the conceptualization and implementation of logistical solutions related to specific hydrocarbons. The incumbent shall serve as a Mentor, Trainer, and Advisor to less experienced Hydrocarbon Schedulers and shall serve as a Back-Up to other Senior or Lead Hydrocarbon Schedulers. Additionally, the incumbent shall promote the study, analysis, and development of logistics optimization activities for his/her specific hydrocarbons individually and, where applicable, in close coordination with the positions of Dock Coordination Manager and the Logistics Analyst, as well as the Lead Hydrocarbon Scheduler. The routine expectations of the job shall include, a) the coordination of CITGO's logistical assets for a specific hydrocarbon to satisfy internal and external customer needs and maximize equipment utilization and efficiency, b) Managing the scheduling of specific hydrocarbon inputs and/or outputs to the refineries, terminals and lube plants, as the case may be, c) Assisting in the formulation of supply and distribution strategies to support margin capture initiatives, demurrage expense reduction, etc. Duties include receiving, reviewing, and consolidating customer notifications and preparing corresponding schedules, analyzing demand and providing scheduling, coordination, recordkeeping, and inventory control for CITGO systems across the supply chain for a specific hydrocarbon commodity.

Job Duties

1. At any given time, the Senior Hydrocarbon Scheduler should have a well-defined scope of work for specific hydrocarbons and a network of internal and external contacts across the supply chain for the specific hydrocarbon commodity under his/her scope of responsibility. The Senior Hydrocarbon Scheduler is a key member of the specific hydrocarbon supply team, and as such should develop work processes to strengthen the coordination with all the key team members involved. For any given hydrocarbon, the Senior Hydrocarbon Scheduler should analyze the forecasted supply/demand requirements, identifying opportunities to: a) optimize inventories within the operating targets established by the specific hydrocarbon Management, b) develop an optimized hydrocarbon movement schedule for each transportation mode required by the circumstances, c) reduce cost and potential inefficiencies, d) jointly optimize use of dock availability and tank space, e) alert the supply team as to potential conflicts and highlight potential solutions, etc. The Senior Hydrocarbon Scheduler should apply expert knowledge of operations, financial processes, and their interrelationships to act as an internal consultant to the respective hydrocarbon supply team.
2. Based on actual execution, forecasted hydrocarbon commodity needs and facility availability, the Senior Hydrocarbon Scheduler should proactively and continually assess and execute solutions to optimize working capital, including physical and in-transit inventory within a deep understanding of the trade-offs between supply and financial impacts, as well as advise on supply contingency plans in face to major events, like major planned and unplanned facility turnarounds, hurricane preparedness, etc.
3. The Senior Hydrocarbon Scheduler should use his/her understanding of the trading cycles and contractual nomination and purchasing rights and obligations to optimize the development and confirmation of the supply programs for the specific hydrocarbons under his/her responsibility. The nominations or purchases should be produced and revised as the case may be, in full concert and alignment with the needs of internal and external customers, which may include, but not limited to, Traders, Corporate Refinery Coordinators, Lead Hydrocarbon Schedulers, Refinery or Origin and Destination schedulers, Terminals, Inspection companies, etc. The Senior Hydrocarbon Scheduler should develop and implement evaluation tools and data collection processes to remain abreast of process performance and communicate results with concrete recommendations.

Job Duties II

4. The Senior Hydrocarbon Scheduler should always be looking beyond the routine aspect of the job to help identify technological solutions leading to higher efficiency, meaningful data collection and data management, process improvements, etc. Compile and maintain accurate hydrocarbon movement and inventory information in SAP. Verify and authorize payment of invoices related to hydrocarbon movement to expedite reconciliation process.
5. The Senior Hydrocarbon Scheduler should partner with the Lead Hydrocarbon Scheduler, Dock Coordination Manager, the Logistics Analyst, and the other members of the Scheduling team to proactively participate on special projects requiring his/her expertise, like the implementation of SAP upgrades, testing of new IT solutions (as an example, related to the Mid Office initiative, etc.), the scheduling implementation around new logistical solutions, like leased storage tanks, docks, or blending facilities, etc.

Minimum Qualifications

• This is a ladder progression for an accomplished professional career hydrocarbon scheduler with a minimum of College Degree and 2 years of combined scheduling, vessel operations, barge and/or rail and freight operations experience preferred or a minimum of a College Degree and 2 years related petroleum industry experience.
• Strong computer skills & excellent math skills
• 24 hr availability – cell phone
• Good oral and written communication skills
• Ability to execute multiple tasks in a fast pace, high stress environment.
• Excellent decision implementation skills
• SAP experience preferred

Job duties displayed above are not all-inclusive, site-specific responsibilities may be assigned.

title: Manager, Credit Risk Governance
description:
Key Responsibilities

Operational Risk Framework for Credit Risk and Stressed Asset Risk (SAR)
• Own and oversee the monthly Operational Risk assessment processes, maintain and update the Credit Risk Register and Risk and Control Self-Assessment for both Credit Risk and SAR.
• Facilitate the completion of Control Tests (KCIs/CSTs) and other governance and control checks. Assist to identify and assess key operational risk areas and control gaps.
• Engage in periodic trigger reviews, Inherent and Residual Risk Assessments, Risk register reviews, risk acceptances, control documents and other regular assessments and ensure that outcomes are appropriately reflected in the relevant governance and reporting systems.
• Investigate exceptions, maintain supporting evidence, track remediation, and escalate material or overdue matters where required.
• Address data-quality issues and support the ongoing maintenance and accuracy of governance records.

Prudential Compliance Framework
• Maintain and update the PCF register for the applicable regulatory requirements (i.e. CRR, PRA Rulebook, PRA Supervisory Statements, and EBA Technical Standards) where Credit Risk RFO is the chapter owner
• Coordinate attestation / confirmation of the articles assigned to the various line owners as part of the quarterly and annual attestation exercise. The attestation/confirmation should be supported by a ‘deep dive’ review, which would entail obtaining documentary evidence for a sample of requirements to confirm that controls and control assurance methods documented in the compliance registers are working effectively;
• Identify appropriate line owner(s) for each changed regulation and ensure timely escalation of regulatory changes to the relevant stakeholders;
• Facilitate annual attestation and quarterly confirmation by CRO CIB Risk / delegate as Chapter Owner by providing them the result of the acceptance by line owners, any material regulatory changes, and gaps/breaches (if any), for onward submission to Group Compliance;
• Ensure that control and assurance methods documented by line owners provide a sufficiently robust control framework to enable effective ongoing compliance, including exception monitoring / reporting;
• Prepare Prudential Regulatory Compliance (Credit Risk) report semi-annually covering the yearly attestation, issues encountered during the exercise and plan/s to resolve with clear timelines for submission to Credit Risk Committee;
• Co-ordinate/support the management of audits relevant to Prudential Compliance;

ICAAP and Regulatory Capital

• Coordinate the annual Credit Risk ICAAP Pillar 2A assessment process.
• Review proposed Credit Risk Pillar 2A capital add-ons and supporting RWA and capital narratives and maintain supporting methodology, analysis, and governance documentation.
• Assess existing and emerging credit risks to determine whether additional Pillar 2A capital may be required.
• Prepare, reconcile, and validate supporting data and perform relevant KCI and CST checks.
• Coordinate stakeholder review and sign-off of Group and Solo ICAAP submissions.
• Prepare materials for Expert Panel reviews, including the methodology review and final capital assessment.

Credit NFRC Governance and Secretariat
• Support the effective operation of the Credit Non-Financial Risk Committee.
• Coordinate agenda setting, meeting timelines, paper submission, pack consolidation, quorum, minutes, and follow-up actions.
• Prepare the committee’s summary and escalation paper.
• Coordinate the annual review of the committee Terms of Reference and the periodic committee effectiveness assessment.
• Review and consolidate relevant Credit NFRC papers and management information, including EA and covenant reporting, SAR KCI reporting, Credit KCI reporting, quarterly KCI and CST exceptions, and policy exceptions.

Other Responsibilities
• Coordinate the annual and periodic review of intragroup outsourcing arrangements.
• Maintain SAR delegated authority letters and coordinate updates to relevant systems when there are changes.
• Support Senior Credit Secretariat requests on SCS Sole/Dual approval process when required
• Support the team with various reports such as Headcount reporting, Conduct dashboard etc.
• Responsible to update the Conduct outcomes and Conflict of Interest register in discussion with Group Compliance
• Perform other credit governance activities and other projects, as assigned

Processes
• Support Credit RFO / Credit PU owner in supervising the Credit Processes.
• Ensure compliance with applicable internal policies, and external laws and regulations, related to Credit Risk.
• Continuously improve the operational efficiency and effectiveness of the risk management processes.

People & Talent
• Lead through example and demonstrate the appropriate culture and values within the function and across the wider organisation.
Risk Management
• Maintain a good understanding of the requirements of key external stakeholders in respect of risk management and ensure these are well understood internally and reflected in internal procedures.
• Obtain assurance regarding the effectiveness of the policy controls and compliance with applicable laws & regulations.
• Maintain an open and cooperative relationship in dealings with internal and external stakeholders

Governance
• Responsible for ensuring effective Risk Governance

Regulatory & Business Conduct
• Display exemplary conduct and live by the Group’s Values and Code of Conduct.
• Take personal responsibility for embedding the highest standards of ethics, including regulatory and business conduct, across Standard Chartered Bank. This includes understanding and ensuring compliance with, in letter and spirit, all applicable laws, regulations, guidelines and the Group Code of Conduct.
• Support the Credit policy team to achieve the outcomes set out in the Bank’s Conduct Principles
• Effectively and collaboratively identify, escalate, mitigate and resolve risk, conduct and compliance matters.
Key stakeholders
• Credit Approvers
• Relationship Managers / COO Office
• Enterprise Risk Management
• SAG/ SAR
• CCRO / Country Credit Governance teams
• Treasury
• CIC Modelling
• Credit Risk Control (Middle Office)
• Credit Risk Infrastructure
• Traded Risk Management
• Operational Risk
• Group Internal Audit
• Legal
• Compliance

Other Responsibilities

Skills and Experience

• Credit Risk Governance
• Operational Risk Controls
• Stakeholder Management
• Strong analytical, communication and interpersonal skills.
• Regulations impacting Credit Risk

Qualifications

• Strong knowledge of credit risk governance
• Experience in governance and control testing, risk registers, RCSA, KCI/CST monitoring, and issue remediation.
• Has good understanding of operating risk identification process and implementing process controls. Experience in working / implementing such methodology in process operations would be preferable.
• Understanding of Basel requirements, regulatory capital, ICAAP, and Pillar 2A and their impact on credit policy, processes, controls, and systems.
• Experience supporting senior governance committees and preparing executive-level papers, management information, and presentations.
• Strong analytical skills, including the ability to review capital and RWA information, reconcile data, challenge assumptions, and identify material issues.
• Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate complex regulatory and risk matters into clear governance documentation.

The General Manager at Action Property Management is a dynamic leader who oversees the daily operations and overall management of a premier residential community. This role is pivotal in fostering strong relationships with homeowners, Board members, and on-site teams while ensuring the property’s standards align with Action’s core values and service excellence. The General Manager leads with integrity, strategic vision, and a commitment to continuous improvement, driving exceptional client satisfaction and operational efficiency.

Ideal Candidate

The ideal candidate will have a minimum of 2–3 years of hands-on HOA community management experience, with a preference for individuals who have supported new-development communities, new construction, or properties transitioning from the development phase to homeowner occupancy.

This individual should possess strong resident-relations and conflict-resolution skills, with the ability to effectively navigate homeowner concerns, foster positive community relationships, and support the successful operations of a growing 55+ single-family home community.

  • Keen knowledge of budgets and the budgeting process.
  • Strong knowledge of audits, reserve studies, bidding process, and Association governing documents.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills.
  • Effective presentation skills.
  • Exceptional time management skills and ability to work independently.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead, mentor, and develop on-site staff to foster a collaborative, high-performing work environment.
  • Ensure team adherence to company policies, procedures, and performance standards.
  • Serve as the primary liaison between the Board of Directors, homeowners, and Action Property Management.

  • Develop and manage annual budgets, monitor financial performance, and ensure timely payment processing.
  • Negotiate, oversee, and evaluate vendor contracts to ensure quality service and cost efficiency.
  • Ensure compliance with all local, state, federal regulations, and company policies.
  • Promote community engagement through events, communications, and homeowner outreach.

title: Substation Department Manager (Columbus Substation Dept)
description:
The WSP Power and Energy (P&E) Power Delivery Substation Business Unit is accepting applications for a Department Manager (DM) for the Substation Department in Columbus, OH reporting to the Midwest Vice President, Region Manager.

This Opportunity

The DM is responsible for managing the day-to-day activities of the department to produce a product consistent with WSP’s mission statement and our culture. The DM is expected to achieve the goals of the department business plan, maintain WSP’s high-quality standards, promote internal teamwork (intra- and inter-department), and support the needs of our clients. This position is also responsible for assisting with developing, maintaining, and strengthening client relationships associated with projects in the department while supporting corporate initiatives in line with department business plan goals. This individual will manage a team of drafters, designers and engineers. The DM is responsible for working closely with the Vice President, Region Manager (VPRM) and other DMs in the region to accomplish regional strategy goals and to balance direct-award "alliance" client backlog while pursuing competitive-bid local work.

WSP brings global expertise in power delivery, power generation, and program management—anchored by the acquisition of POWER Engineers, Inc. TRC Companies have now joined WSP, deepening our power practice and expanding our energy advisory and intelligent grid services. We're partnering with clients to shape how energy systems evolve around the world—and we need your help.

Your Impact

  • Act as trusted advisor to the VPRM to support the Midwest Region, communicating regularly via: Touchpoints, Region teleconferences, Monthly reporting, Region meetings (travel may be required), Plan audits, Department Manager meetings (travel may be required)
  • Manage all financial, technical, and staffing aspects of performance for this Substation Department, including, but not limited to: Employee timecard approvals, Employee expense approvals, Financial reporting, Weekly and monthly resource planning, Business plans, Employee appraisals, Salary/promotion/bonus recommendations, Department participation in training, Proposals, Project design book audits, Lunch & learns, Mentorship, QA/QC.
  • Apply high-level substation engineering techniques and processes to identify improvements for various infrastructure project phases including concept development, preliminary design, final design, procurement, construction, and operation.
  • Develop construction plans, specifications, and cost estimates; preparing construction safety and phasing plans and updating infrastructure layout plans that require coordination with owners, other disciplines, sub-consultants, and clients.
  • Develop and incorporate advanced technologies, monitoring devices, building materials, modeling techniques, design requirements.
  • Oversee and monitor cross-functional teams of engineers and scientific professionals to execute project work on mid-level and/or multiple concurrent projects, including budgets, tracking hours and expenses, task completion, cost and quantities of materials/equipment/labor, technical calculations, construction, compliance documentation, and regulatory and technical analysis memos.
  • Prepare comprehensive technical reports and presentations that explain research, concepts, and recommendations to prevent, control, restore, or address structural, environmental, design, and/or construction issues or opportunities.
  • Proactively collaborate with other engineers, professionals, and leaders on proposal and business development opportunities.
  • Remain current in latest substation engineering techniques and practices.
  • Exercise responsible and ethical decision-making regarding company funds, resources and conduct, and adhere to WSP’s Code of Conduct and related policies and procedures.
  • Perform additional responsibilities as required by business needs.

Who You Are

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Engineering, or closely related discipline (or equivalent experience).
  • 7 to 10+ years of relevant post education experience in engineering discipline and prior design experience.
  • Demonstratable experience as a leader of project and/or client teams.
  • Demonstrated competence in client team development and growing/maintaining client relationships.
  • Proficient with electrical engineering principles, practices, process, design/build, and the application to project work-related issues.
  • Well-defined specific knowledge of relevant electrical codes, regulations, compliance practices, and record-keeping requirements.
  • Well-developed ability to make technical computations and calculations involving the application of engineering principles, understanding plans and specifications, and making factual comparisons to the appropriate regulations.
  • Highly effective interpersonal and communication skills when interacting with others, expressing ideas effectively and professionally to an engineering and non-engineering audience.
  • Demonstrated high-level of self-leadership with attention to detail, multi-tasking, and prioritization of responsibilities in a dynamic work environment.
  • Works independently with minimal oversight and provides guidance and leadership to junior team or project members, with strict adherence to QA/QC.
  • Proficient with technical writing, office automation, discipline-specific design software (i.e., MicroStation, AutoCAD, MS Office, etc), technology, math principles, spreadsheets, and tools.
  • Well-developed critical thinking and problem-solving skills required to apply technical knowledge to reach conclusions from testing results, data collation, computations, statistical analysis and arriving at the most effective, economical, and logical solution.
  • Proven track record of upholding workplace safety and ability to abide by WSP’s health, safety and drug/alcohol and harassment policies.
  • Ability to work schedules conducive to project-specific requirements that may extend beyond the typical workweek.
  • Occasional travel may be required depending on project-specific requirements.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 2+ years of experience as a people leader in a management capacity.
  • Professional Engineer License.
  • Demonstrated Competence in working with other WSP Departments

* Experience in bare-metal firmware development for embedded systems

* Demonstrated adaptability, agility, and the ability to innovate under pressure to meet dynamic project demands and drive successful outcomes.
* Classroom or project experience in developing code (Verilog, VHDL) for FPGAs

At Curium, we have a singular focus – to develop, manufacture, and supply world-class radiopharmaceutical products around the globe. We strive to innovate further in nuclear diagnostics and therapies so we can enhance the lives of people with cancer.

Requirements

  • Previous experience in an IT environment/company or an administrative position
  • Good working knowledge of Microsoft Excel

  • Experience supporting large or cross-functional teams

title: Operator III (Machine Shop)
description:
Eaton’s EPG CHD EP Americas division is currently seeking a Operator III (Machine Shop).

The hourly rate for this position is $21.90 per hour.

Please note the salary information shown above is a general guideline only. Salaries are based upon candidate skills, experience, and qualifications, as well as market and business considerations.

What you’ll do:

PRIMARY FUNCTION:
This position is responsible for setting up and operating conventional, special-purpose, and numerical control (NC) machines and machining centers to fabricate metallic and non-metallic parts. The incumbent will also fit and assemble machine parts into complete units, applying knowledge of machine shop theory and procedures, shop mathematics, machinability of materials, and layout techniques.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:
1. Studies blueprints, sketches, drawings, manuals, specifications, and sample parts to determine dimensions and tolerances of finished workpiece, sequence of operations, or setup requirements
2. Measures, marks, and scribes dimensions and reference points on material or workpiece as guides for subsequent machining
3. Selects, aligns, and secures holding fixtures, cutting tools, attachments, accessories, and materials on machines; such as mills, lathes, jig borers, grinders, and shapers
4. Calculates and sets controls to regulate machining factors such as speed, feed, coolant flow, and dept and angle of cut; or enters commands to retrieve, input, or edit computerized machine control media
5. Starts and observes machine operations to detect malfunctions and out-of-tolerance machining, and adjusts machine controls or control media as required
6. Verifies conformance of finished workpiece to specifications, using precision measuring instruments
7. Sets up and operates machine on trial run to verify accuracy of machine settings or programmed control data
8. Fits and assembles parts into complete assembly using jigs, fixtures, surface plate, surface table, hand tools, and power tools
9. Verifies dimensions and alignment of assembly, using measuring instruments such as micrometers, height gauges, and gauge blocks
10. May develop specifications from general description and draw sketch of part or product to be fabricated
11. May confer with engineers, production personnel, programmers, or others to resolve machining or assembly problems
12. Performs other duties as assigned

Qualifications:

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:
1. Must be legally authorized to work in the US without company sponsorship
2. Must have a high school diploma or GED from an accredited institution
3. Understanding of basic CNC control functions, machining, and basic math functions
4. Minimum of 2 years experience in a multiple process-manufacturing environment
5. Knowledge of various measuring instruments and ability to read blueprints.
6. This position requires use of information or access to hardware which is subject to the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR). All applications must be US persons within the meaning of ITAR. ITAR defines a US person as a US Citizen, US Permanent Resident (i.e. “Green Card Holder”), Political Asylee, or Refugee
7. Remain standing for an extended period of time up to 8 hours
8. Able to lift to 35 lbs. on a regular basis

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:
1. Two years of work experience in a machine shop

  • Conduct on-site admission and initial intake interviews of youth to include gathering familial, possible sponsorship information and to establish age of the youth.

  • Conduct interviews of sponsors/family members, friends of family to vet sponsor’s ability to care for the minor(s).

  • Act as UC case POC for assigned Federal Field Specialist, Case Coordinator and Contract Field Specialist.

  • Prepare case for, conduct and lead pre staffing process with multidisciplinary team of professionals including case managers, clinical counselors, medical coordinators and other designated stakeholders.

  • Attend staffing(s) with Case Coordinators, Federal Field Specialists and other ORR stakeholders as needed.

  • Coordinate with local pro bono attorneys for the timely provision of “Know Your Rights” presentations and legal screenings to children in care.

  • Work with program administration, clinical, medical and educational staff in identifying best case management practices while maintaining a collaborative multi-disciplinary environment.

  • Work to ensure children in care are provided a safe environment and safe and timely release from ORR care pursuant to ORR MAP Section 2; this may include completing online address searches, obtaining birth certificates to prove relationship, income verifications, background checks, and other actions to ensure proper vetting of the Sponsor, household members and adult caregivers.

  • Document all actions taken and contacts with youth, sponsor, and stakeholders in the form of progress notes as required by NYAP.

  • Complete and submit reunification packets and Release Requests for initial review to Lead Case Manager or Program designee.

  • Submit completed reunification packet with appropriate referral made by Case Manager for the timely release of youth to designated sponsor, including referrals for home studies and post release services (PRS).

  • Provide weekly face to face updates to youth and telephonic updates to family members/sponsor.

  • Ensure the provision of two weekly telephonic contacts with family in the US or COO, primary caregiver and/or sponsor.

  • Facilitate incoming calls to minors with the appropriate family members and other approved caregivers.

  • Facilitate attorney to client contact as requested by youth.

  • Coordinate weekly treatment team meetings with representatives from all departments at the Program.

  • Establish and maintain a strong relationship with assigned foster parents, attend meetings with foster parents and act as program liaison with foster caregivers.

  • Drive children to facilitate program services, may include transportation to court appointments, attorney visits, other appointments as needed per contractual duties; this may also include transporting youth within the United States for reunification purposes.

  • Coordinate case management and family reunification services for children, including active involvement in discharge planning.

  • Actively participate in documenting safety plans and Post 18 age out plans.

  • Oversee and/ or actively participate in the process of reporting significant incidents (SIRs) in accordance with existing policies and procedures.

  • Ensure maintenance of UC electronic and physical files, including uploading documents in UC Portal, Evolve, and maintaining the corresponding physical file.

  • Perform other duties as assigned.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor’s degree required in Social Work, Psychology, Human Services, Counseling or other social service field. One (1) year experience preferred working with children and adolescents or in the youth services field. (volunteer and internship experienced included).

  • Excellent case management, verbal and written communication skills. Critical assessment and analysis skills. Motivated, organized, flexible and able to navigate multiple service priorities. Ability to work under stress and multitasking.

  • Must demonstrate a sincere commitment to the service and advocacy for youth and families

  • Required to work a flexible schedule to facilitate program services, including working on call schedules which includes weekends and evenings.

  • Cleared Level II background check from appropriate entity.

  • Must be able to obtain Crisis Prevention Institute (CPI) certification and First Aid Certification (CPR).

  • Must be able to supervise clients indoors and outdoors as necessary.

  • Proficient use of desktop and laptop computers, smartphones and tablets, printers, fax machines, and photocopiers, as well as software including word processing, spreadsheet, and database programs.

  • Bilingual (English/Spanish). Fluency in Spanish is required.

  • Minimum automobile insurance coverage of $100,000/300,000 bodily liability coverage.

  • 21 years of age, a valid state driver’s license, a reliable personal vehicle, and a good driving record.

OTHER SKILLS

  • A willingness to work flexible and non-traditional hours in the service of foster caregivers, families of origin, and persons served.

  • Must be able to work 8 UC cases with minimal supervision but may increase depending on sponsor category and other factors.

  • Attending all organizational required trainings.

  • Attending all departmental and program meetings to ensure that up-to-date information is received and/or information on policy changes or practices is adhered to.

  • Attending training that will enhance professional growth in case manager and documentation or other topics as deemed appropriate by the program director.

  • Must assist in the evacuation of youth as needed due to inclement weather conditions, natural disasters, or other unforeseen occurrences.

  • Travel as needed for trainings, conferences or to transport youth to destinations located within the U.S.

  • Maintain a safe, clean and hazard-free work area.

  • Follow ORR, CDC, and State Covid 19 related protocols.

  • Ensure the proper supervision of youth at all times.

  • Able to react to change productively and handle other essential tasks as assigned.

  • Capacity to be flexible and responsive to youth served, foster caregivers, system partners, and internal/external stakeholders.

  • Capacity to remain objective and professional in all areas of job function.

  • Demonstrates tolerance and respect for the ideas and actions of others.

  • Possess a sincere desire and ability to advocate for children facing behavioral health, immigration, educational, legal, development, and socio-economic challenges.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS

  • Use of manual dexterity, tactile, visual, and audio acuity.

  • Use of repetitive motion, prolonged periods of sitting and standing, and sustained visual and mental applications and demands.

  • Occasional lifting (up to 25 pounds), bending, pulling, and carrying.

  • Ability to travel frequently and drive vehicle while sitting for extended periods, with frequency varying based on program demands.

  • Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the job.

title: Director of Development & Strategic Alumni Engagement
description:
Classification Title:

Director of Development & Strategic Alumni Engagement

Classification Minimum Requirements:

Masters degree in appropriate area of specialization and three years of appropriate experience in Development or a related field; or a bachelors degree in appropriate areas of specialization and five years of experience in Development or a related field.

Job Description:

**Portfolio Management**

- Manage and strategically grow a portfolio of major gift prospects donors (rated from $100,000 and above).
- Responsible for identifying and building relationships with prospects through face-to-face visits and developing cultivation strategies.
- Develop and execute individualized cultivation and solicitation strategies aligned with college funding priorities.
- Partner with faculty and college leadership to align donor interests with institutional initiatives.
- Identify and develop relationships with private, family and corporate foundations whose philanthropic priorities align with college initiatives; coordinate strategy, proposal development, cultivation, stewardship, and reporting in partnerships with college leadership and UF Advancement.
- Develop and execute a comprehensive engagement and programming strategy that advances the College’s priorities across its **s** ix key stakeholder audiences: alumni, donors, students, parents/families, faculty/staff, and corporate/community partners.
- Partner with the College’s corporate relations leadership to identify, research, qualify, and prioritize corporations and corporate foundations whose philanthropic, workforce, talent, community engagement, or strategic priorities align with the College of Nursing.
- Manage Dean’s Circle of Excellence, including solicitation and stewardship of members.
- Coordinate major gift outreach activities, including stewardship.
- Record and manage all donor activity within the Advance database; ensure accurate prospect tracking and pipeline management.
- Analyze giving trends and prepare strategic reports and presentations for leadership.
- Proactively identify new major gift and planned giving prospects through research and strategic engagement efforts.

**Alumni Affairs Efforts**

- Identify, develop, pilot and evaluate new approaches to alumni engagement and donor experience using constituent insights and data.
- Establish new programs to engage alumni with faculty and students.
- Track, measures and reports on all alumni engagement activities.
- Partner with communications staff to oversee alumni-facing communications (website, social media, newsletters, email, and video content).
- Plan and produces select alumni engagement events.
- Work closely with UF Alumni Relations staff to coordinate alumni affairs efforts across UF.

**Event Strategy & Donor Stewardship**

- Assist in identifying award recipients for annual donor recognition event and Dorothy M. Smith Leadership Awards.
- Work with Senior Director on script and presentation for the Donor Recognition Event.
- Support the strategic planning and execution of donor recognition and stewardship events, including the annual Donor Recognition Event and leadership award programs.
- Serve as a host and advancement representative at college and university events.
- Oversee pre- and post-event donor engagement and follow-up communications.
- Collaborate on the design and development of event collateral, pledge materials, and stewardship communications.
- Participate in university events and serve on volunteer committees as needed.
- Work with Development Coordinator on scholarship Thank You notes for donors.
- Connect alumni, cultivation, recognition, and stewardship events to broader advancement objectives through defined audiences, relationship goals, pre-event strategy, post-event follow up, and appropriate measures of success.

**Quality Assurance**

- Ensure best practices in office systems, files and record keeping.
- Ensure effective use of strategic tools and resources such as contact reports, prospect management, research and analysis, and the Advance database.
- Plan and monitor the budget, using resources for best results in fundraising and planning activities involving volunteers, prospects, faculty, and administration.

Expected Salary:

$90-105k commensurate on education and experience.

Required Qualifications:

Masters degree in appropriate area of specialization and three years of appropriate experience in Development or a related field; or a bachelors degree in appropriate areas of specialization and five years of experience in Development or a related field.

Valid Drivers License is required.

Preferred:

- Three to five years of major gift fundraising experience with proven success soliciting gifts of $25,000 and above strongly preferred.
- Related experience working with volunteers and/or in similar organization.
- Enthusiasm for fundraising in a comprehensive research university and the desire to work collegially within a goal-oriented fundraising organization.
- Knowledge of fundraising principles, methods, and standards.
- Expertise in developing solicitation strategies.
- The ability to work strategically, develop and implement constituency programs and activities, along with a talent for motivating volunteers.
- Ability to work collaboratively and as a team player
- Competency in problem solving.
- Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, strong interpersonal abilities, and the capacity to engage effectively and collaboratively with a wide range of individuals are essential.
- Support the University’s commitment to creating a respectful and collaborative work environment that values integrity, professionalism, and mutual respect in all interactions; demonstrated success collaborating with stakeholders; strong project management skills; experience in a data-driven environment; excellent organizational abilities; and the capacity to lead, influence, and inspire others are essential.
- Proficient in the following areas: Windows operating systems, Microsoft Word, Excel, and Access, as well as internet browsers and email platforms. Familiarity with donor databases, contact management systems, and tracking systems is also highly preferred.
- The ability and willingness to travel.  A valid driver license and good driving record are essential.*

title: Medical Liaison - Sickle Cell Disease / Hemoglobinopathies  - Florida
description:
About the Department

The Clinical, Medical and Regulatory (CMR) department at Novo Nordisk is one of the most diverse and collaborative groups within the organization. From healthcare provider interactions and developing and implementing regulatory strategies with the FDA to providing medical education and collecting data to support efficacy and new product development, CMR is involved. The one thing that keeps us all marching to the same beat is our patient centered focus. At Novo Nordisk, you will help patients around the world. As their needs evolve, so does our challenge to find better and more innovative ways to improve their quality of life. We’re changing lives for a living. Are you ready to make a difference?

The Position

Builds relationships with HCPs and demonstrates the clinical outcomes of NNI Hemoglobinopathies portfolio. Educates and demonstrates the safety and efficacy of key products to HCPs. Provides medical information and coordinates educational workshops, round tables, medical forums, etc.. May explore and identify sites for clinical trials in all stages of development. Incumbents have a deep scientific and clinical education and experience. Within Field Medical Affairs, this position functions as a scientific liaison between NNI and key external customers to further scientific exchange. S/he provides advanced product and scientific and medical field support to Medical, Sales and Marketing, as well as Managed Care and Government by using academic/professional credentials and scientific expertise to communicate with health care providers, organized providers/accounts and other relevant healthcare organizations. Strategic determination of change of territory prioritization will be based on customer need and analytics which identify need for change. This may occur at any time throughout the annual performance cycle. Develops and maintains medical (territory and account) plans in coordination with his/her Field Director.

Relationships

Position reports to Field Director/Sr Field Director. Serves as organization spokesperson on advanced medical and technical projects with the ML teams, Clinicians, Marketing, Market Access & Government and Sales personnel. External relationships include key opinion leaders (KOL’s), academic institutions, physicians, nurse practitioners, diabetes educators, pharmacists, blood bank staff, organized providers/IDNs and MCOs as needed based on territory archetypes.

Essential Functions

  • Administrative Duties:
    • Completes administrative duties in an accurate manner and on a timely basis, in line with current SOPs and working practices
    • Complies with all guidelines, policies, legal, regulatory and compliance requirements
    • Ensures effective administrative management of regional business as well as operational budgets
    • Maintains thorough understanding of all relevant Novo Nordisk processes and procedures and proactively assists other FMA members to further their understanding with these as needed
    • Provides monthly reports on scientific support activities in region to Director including budget expenditures as directed
    • Records all activities within a customer response management system (e.g. VEEVA) and all expenses within Concur in accordance with FMA procedures
  • Advocacy & Professional Relationship Development:
    • Attends assigned medical and scientific meetings: a) ensures and maintains awareness of current issues and new data pertaining to NNI products; b) develops and maintains relationships with key health care providers and IHNs; c) develops appropriate use of NNI products and greater utilization of its services d) supports and assists representatives and managers in answering questions from health care providers and IHNs
    • Combines account management skills, business acumen and scientific expertise to enhance value and develop collaborative relationships
    • Establishes the medical account strategy/plan through the identification and cultivation of key relationships and brings forth appropriate collaboration opportunities
  • Field-Based Clinical Support:
    • Collaborates with Health Economics & Outcomes Research (HEOR) team to deliver scientific value proposition of NNI’s products and devices to key customers and formulary decision makers. Delivers HEOR presentations upon request
    • Collaborates with Marketing and Sales management to inform the development of scientific strategies to optimize NNI’s products and development activities in the medical community
    • Collaborates with trial/study investigation sites; ensuring effective coordination and facilitation of studies to ensure timely review, initiation and completion, as well as publication of study results. Provides clinical support in cooperation with other Novo Nordisk groups to ensure investigators demonstrate appropriate knowledge of studies, support patient recruitment and retention activities, answers responsive requests from investigators and provides feedback to sites to other groups
    • Coordinates and collaborates with regional FMA team members to ensure integrated comprehensive coverage of regional clinical and scientific needs
    • Coordinates with key internal stakeholders to provide customized and dedicated system-wide clinical education and support within respective IHNs and coordinate and manage professional relations of Novo Nordisk within these Networks from an overall “account management” level
    • Coordinates with respective HSM to provide scientific and clinical education to Chief Executives, Medical Directors and formulary stakeholders to secure proper access to NNI’s products and services in respective IHNs
    • Develops and presents product and scientific updates as requested, including Formulary presentations within IHNs, using approved material

Physical Requirements

  • 50-75% overnight travel required.
  • The territory for this position is: Florida
  • Position is Field Based and the ideal candidate must live within the territory or in a bordering state located near a major airport.
  • Driver must maintain a valid driver’s license. Must be in good standing by not exceeding the Novo Nordisk points threshold assigned based on review of Motor Vehicle Records.

Qualifications

  • Doctoral degree required
  • At least two years’ experience in a health-related system, pharmaceutical company, or managed care environment required
  • Relevant clinical and/or therapeutic experience preferred
  • Displays business acumen/knowledge based on experiences such as participation in formulary process decisions
  • Extensive experience in Sickle Cell Disease / Hemoglobinopathies strongly preferred
  • Strong communication skills

This position is part of a job family. Title and level within the job family are evaluated based on a number of factors, such as years of experience, scope of work, proficiency and business need. Candidates will be assessed for the most appropriate title and level within the job family during the recruitment process. The base range of pay for each title in this job family are as follows:

Medical Liaison - $170,000 to $215,000
Senior Medical Liaison - $198,000 to $245,000

In addition, this position is eligible for a company bonus based on individual and company performance. Novo Nordisk offers long-term incentive compensation and or company vehicles depending on the position's level or other company factors.

Employees are also eligible to participate in Company employee benefit programs including medical, dental and vision coverage; life insurance; disability insurance; 401(k) savings plan; flexible spending accounts; employee assistance program; tuition reimbursement program; and voluntary benefits such as group legal, critical illness, identity theft protection, pet insurance and auto/home insurance. The Company also offers time off pursuant to its sick time policy, flex-able vacation policy and parental leave policy.

We commit to an inclusive recruitment process and equality of opportunity for all our job applicants.

At Novo Nordisk, we're not chasing quick fixes – we're creating lasting change for long-term health. Job Summary

General Atomics (GA), and its affiliated companies, is one of the world’s leading resources for high-technology systems development ranging from the nuclear fuel cycle to remotely piloted aircraft, airborne sensors, and advanced electric, electronic, wireless and laser technologies.

The Identity and Access Management (IAM) System Administrator manages user accounts, access privileges, and authentication services across Information Assurance systems. This position supports platforms such as SailPoint, Active Directory, Okta, PowerShell-based automation, and other internal identity-management tools.

The administrator is responsible for account provisioning, modification, suspension, and termination; access reviews; identity lifecycle management; troubleshooting; documentation; and compliance with security policies and system requirements.

**DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:**

- Create, modify, disable, and delete user accounts based on approved requests and established procedures.
- Process account-management activities through approved ticketing systems and workflow tools.
- Validate account requests and confirm that all required approvals are documented before making changes.
- Assign and update user roles, group memberships, permissions, and access levels in accordance with business requirements and least-privilege principles.
- Support onboarding, transfers, and offboarding activities in coordination with Human Resources, Security, Information Technology, system owners, and management.
- Support password resets, account unlocks, multifactor authentication enrollment, and other access-related services.
- Monitor and support user identity lifecycle events across identity and access management platforms.
- Maintain accurate account inventories, access records, audit trails, and supporting documentation.
- Conduct periodic access reviews and assist with identifying inactive, duplicate, excessive, or unauthorized accounts.
- Monitor account activity and escalate suspicious or potentially unauthorized access in accordance with established procedures.
- Troubleshoot account and authentication issues and coordinate with system owners, service desk personnel, and other support teams as needed.
- Use PowerShell and other approved tools to automate account-management activities and process bulk requests or jobs.
- Support audits, assessments, investigations, and compliance reporting.
- Develop, maintain, and follow standard operating procedures, work instructions, and account-management documentation.
- Identify opportunities for process improvement and recommend enhancements to increase accuracy, efficiency, and security and consult with direct manager first before implementing.
- Protect sensitive, personally identifiable, proprietary, and company information.
- Manage assigned work and, when applicable, coordinate or take/assign more work from the main ticketing system dedicated to Account Admin team.
- Perform other duties as assigned by management.
- Meet applicable security-clearance eligibility requirements or obtain security clearance, as required for the position.

We recognize and appreciate the value and contributions of individuals with diverse backgrounds and experiences and welcome all qualified individuals to apply.

Job Qualifications

- Typically requires a bachelor's degree in information technology or a related discipline and three or more years of progressive professional systems administration experience in an information technology department primarily in systems administration. May substitute equivalent working experience in the field in lieu of education.
- Experience administering user accounts, access permissions, or identity-management systems.
- Working knowledge of authentication, authorization, role-based access control, and least-privilege principles.
- Familiarity with directory and identity platforms such as Active Directory, Microsoft Entra ID, LDAP, SailPoint, Okta, or comparable systems.
- Basic understanding of account and identity lifecycle management processes.
- Strong attention to detail and the ability to follow documented procedures.
- Effective written and verbal communication skills.
- Ability to manage multiple requests while meeting service-level, operational, and security requirements.
- Ability to handle confidential and sensitive information appropriately.
- Must have the ability to obtain and maintain a DoD security clearance.

- Experience with identity governance, privileged access management, or multifactor authentication solutions.
- Familiarity with Windows, Linux, cloud, and enterprise application account administration.
- Experience with PowerShell, Python, or other scripting and automation tools.
- Experience supporting account provisioning, deprovisioning, access reviews, or identity governance processes.
- Experience in an aerospace, defense, government-contracting, or other regulated environment.
- Relevant certifications, such as Security+, Microsoft certifications, or identity-and-access-management certifications.

- Account provisioning and access administration
- Security awareness and policy compliance

- Troubleshooting and problem resolution
- Attention to detail

title: LNG Product Engineer
description:
Honeywell Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) combines proven liquefaction technology with decades of equipment design, manufacturing, and operating experience. Our engineering teams design efficient, customizable, and sustainable solutions that help customers liquefy natural gas and move energy more effectively to end users around the world.

Based at Honeywell LNG headquarters in Allentown, PA working on a hybrid work schedule, you will join the Manufacturing & Design Engineering organization and report to the MDE Director. In this highly visible role, you will connect engineering, commercial, supplier, and project teams to create the technical frameworks that keep LNG offerings aligned, executable, and protected.

You will own the tools and technical content that translate our design approach into strong customer contracts and actionable supplier requirements. Your work will improve consistency across bids, projects in execution, and Aftermarket Services offerings while reducing ambiguity, protecting Honeywell intellectual property, and helping technical teams move faster with confidence.

The position will require occasional domestic and international travel to other Honeywell sites, supplier locations, and customer locations

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Create and continuously improve standardized technical exhibits for customer contracts, giving every opportunity a strong starting point grounded in current LNG design practices.
  • Develop reusable technical requisition packages for suppliers and vendors covering modules, cold boxes, pressure vessels, heat exchangers, valves, control systems, instrumentation, third-party design support, and other purchased scope.
  • Connect customer commitments, the internal design basis, and supplier purchase orders so technical requirements remain clear, consistent, and traceable throughout each project.
  • Lead the evolution of LNG’s technical knowledge architecture, including specifications, standards, workflows, calculation templates, design methods, manufacturing guidance, industrial references, and intellectual property.
  • Partner with engineering disciplines to keep technical content current, incorporate lessons learned, and embed approved design-basis changes into reusable deliverables.
  • Support project planning and execution strategies by identifying project-specific customer, regulatory, and industry requirements and helping LNG disciplines apply them accurately.
  • Align Honeywell LNG technical requirements and offerings with adjacent Honeywell Gas and LNG end-to-end capabilities, including pretreatment, controls, and machinery.
  • Coordinate technical questions and close gaps in design-basis or contractual documents, driving issues to practical, timely resolution.

YOU MUST HAVE

  • 10+ years of experience in engineering or technical project execution.
  • Demonstrated understanding of gas and energy industry plant design, technical offerings, and project scope.
  • Ability to coordinate cross-functional technical inquiries and drive gaps in LNG design-basis or contractual documents to resolution.
  • Strong organizational and analytical skills, with the ability to manage multiple urgent priorities through completion.
  • Excellent technical and contractual writing skills.

WE VALUE

  • Bachelor's degree in Engineering
  • You are naturally curious and energized by resolving gaps in technical understanding.
  • You build trust across commercial and engineering disciplines and bring diverse contributors toward a clear outcome.
  • You work efficiently in a dynamic environment, maintain momentum across competing priorities, and communicate risks early.
  • You approach conflict constructively and preserve strong working relationships while protecting technical rigor.
  • You are committed to continuous improvement and invest in your development through training and certification.

BENEFITS OF WORKING FOR HONEYWELL

In addition to a competitive salary, leading-edge work, and developing solutions side-by-side with dedicated experts in their fields, Honeywell employees are eligible for a comprehensive benefits package. This package includes employer subsidized Medical, Dental, Vision, and Life Insurance; Short-Term and Long-Term Disability; 401(k) match, Flexible Spending Accounts, Health Savings Accounts, EAP, and Educational Assistance; Parental Leave, Paid Time Off (for vacation, personal business, sick time, and parental leave), and 12 Paid Holidays. Learn more

The application period for the job is estimated to be 40 days from the job posting date; however, this may be shortened or extended depending on business needs and the availability of qualified candidates. Posted date: November 2nd, 2026.

ABOUT HONEYWELL TECHNOLOGIES

Honeywell Technologies is a global, pure-play automation company with a legacy of innovating to help solve the world’s most mission-critical challenges, enhancing the quality of life for people and communities around the world. We serve the building, industrial, and process sectors with a broad portfolio of services, solutions, and products, underpinned by our Honeywell Technologies Accelerator operating system and Honeywell Technologies Forge intelligence layer. By combining the deep domain expertise of our more than 50,000 employees with decades of data from our global installed base, we are uniquely positioned to lead the industrial sector’s transition from automation to autonomy. Learn more

THE BUSINESS UNIT

Honeywell Technologies Process Automation helps customers run complex industrial operations more safely, efficiently, and reliably. From automation and control systems to cybersecurity, digital solutions, and operational optimization, we enable critical industries to improve performance, reduce risk, and achieve their sustainability objectives.

description:
Come Build Your Career at Aecon!
