title: Plant Health Care Program Specialist
description:
Job Summary

The Plant Health Care Program Specialist is responsible for protecting and improving the health of trees, shrubs, and ornamental plants through professional inspection, diagnosis, treatment, and preventative care. This position provides on-site plant health services at residential and commercial customer properties by identifying insects, diseases, nutrient deficiencies, and environmental stressors while developing and implementing customized treatment plans.

The Plant Health Care Program Specialist performs hands-on treatments, including soil applications, tree injections, trunk injections, foliar sprays, and other Integrated Pest Management (IPM) solutions. In addition to performing treatments, this role documents all findings, treatment recommendations, products applied, and customer interactions to ensure accurate service records and exceptional customer care.

Success in this position requires strong plant health knowledge, attention to detail, excellent communication skills, and a commitment to delivering safe, effective, and environmentally responsible solutions.

Key Duties and Responsibilities

Plant Health Assessments & Treatments

  • Travel to customer properties to perform scheduled plant health evaluations and service appointments, with visits averaging 45–60 minutes.
  • Inspect trees, shrubs, palms, and ornamental plants to identify insects, diseases, nutrient deficiencies, environmental stress, and structural concerns, and determine appropriate treatment recommendations.
  • Perform hands-on plant health treatments, including soil and trunk injections, soil drenches, foliar applications, fertilization, and insect, disease, and preventative treatments.
  • Safely mix, handle, transport, and apply pesticides, fertilizers, and other treatment products in accordance with all federal, state, and local regulations.
  • Perform basic pruning and trimming to support plant health and remove damaged or diseased material when appropriate.

Documentation & Reporting

  • Maintain detailed service records for every customer visit, including inspection findings, treatment recommendations, products applied, application rates, quantities used, service dates, and treatment results.
  • Develop and maintain customized treatment schedules and long-term plant health care plans.
  • Record all services and customer communications within company software and mobile applications.
  • Ensure all pesticide application records and regulatory documentation are accurate and compliant.

Customer Service

  • Build strong relationships with customers through professional communication and exceptional service, explaining findings and recommendations in an easy-to-understand manner.
  • Educate customers on plant health issues, treatment options, and preventative care, and answer questions regarding insects, diseases, tree health, irrigation, fertilization, and seasonal care.
  • Communicate follow-up recommendations and future treatment schedules.
  • Promote additional plant health services when appropriate to improve customer landscapes.

Safety & Compliance

  • Follow all company safety policies and procedures.
  • Comply with all pesticide handling, storage, transportation, and application regulations.
  • Wear appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE) during all treatment applications.
  • Maintain company equipment, spray systems, injection equipment, and service vehicles, and ensure vehicles, equipment, and chemicals are kept in a safe and compliant manner.

This is not an exhaustive list of responsibilities. We work collaboratively and new responsibilities may be assigned over time.

title: Staff or Senior Research Auditor, Office of Audit and Compliance - UT System Administration
description:
The Research Auditor performs risk-based audit, advisory, and compliance activities supporting the University of Tennessee System’s research enterprise. This position evaluates processes, controls, and compliance risks related to sponsored research, research administration, research integrity, and the management of federal, state, and other externally funded research activities and research security.

Responsibilities include assisting with or leading audits and consultations; evaluating compliance with applicable federal and state laws, regulations, sponsor requirements, University policies, and grant terms and conditions; and identifying opportunities to strengthen controls, accountability, and operational effectiveness. The position supports research-focused risk assessments and audit planning by identifying emerging risks and areas of potential noncompliance across the System.

The Research Auditor works collaboratively with Research Administration, principal investigators, departmental leadership, compliance functions, and other University stakeholders. Relevant areas of knowledge or experience include Uniform Guidance; sponsored-project administration; subrecipient monitoring; effort reporting; cost allowability; procurement; financial conflict of interest; research security; export control; human subjects protections; and other research compliance requirements.

A Senior Research Auditor independently leads more complex research-related engagements, develops audit programs and risk assessments, communicates results to senior leadership, and may provide guidance or mentorship to other audit staff.

Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

Project Planning and Management

Develops or oversees development of project plans to achieve objectives, including all areas of the unit’s operations to be examined, the data and information to be gathered, and the methods of data/information gathering to be used. Conducts or oversees risk analyses to define the project objectives, scope, and methodologies. The risk analyses considers the financial, operational, compliance, and/or strategic risks associated with an organizational unit’s operations. Coordinates the work of other team members. Provides needed guidance and instruction to other team members. Assigns work, monitors time budgets and target dates for team member assignments, and monitors project budget and deadlines. Informs supervisor, when applicable, about status of the audit work performed, potential issues and solutions, and client feedback.

Fieldwork Execution and Documentation

Collects and analyzes appropriate types of information, data, and evidence to achieve the objectives of project steps by 1.) Compiling data from the university’s information systems and other sources internal and external to the university, 2.) Applying appropriate sampling techniques, 3.) Collecting documents, 4.) Observing processes and controls, 5.) Preparing for and conducting interviews, 6.) Using questionnaires and surveys 7.) Utilizing data analytics or other methodologies, as needed

Prepares thorough, well-organized, and self-explanatory work papers to support conclusions reached and demonstrate achievement of objectives.

Quality Assurance and Improvement Activities

Provides first or final review of work papers generated by other team members. Reviews reports drafted by other team members to ensure reports are clear, concise, and convey needed information. Evaluates the effectiveness of the audit process at the conclusion of each project. Provides formal feedback to team members at the end of projects. Participates in long-range planning, development of audit tools, and improvements to office practices.

Issue Identification and Resolution

Analyzes data and information gathered or oversees analysis to identify issues, such as ineffectiveness of policies and procedures in addressing risks, areas of noncompliance, inefficiencies of operations, or evidence of fraudulent acts. Identifies potential solutions for significant issues that address any deficiencies or offer operational improvements, ensuring the solutions are cost-effective and feasible to implement.

Client Communication and Audit Reporting

Negotiates with audit clients to arrive at sound/effective recommendations. Apprises client of project status, barriers to progress, and potential issues. Leads entrance and exit conferences. Drafts project reports or reviews reports drafted by team members. Evaluates client’s written responses to recommendations. Clearly conveys information and ideas in a manner that engages the listener or reader, helps them understand and retain the message, and invites response and feedback. Composes and/or modifies communication depending on the targeted audience.

Bachelor's degree in accounting or other related field and more than two years of experience in internal auditing, compliance, information systems auditing, consulting, investigations, Uniform Guidance, sponsored project administration, subsequent monitoring, effort reporting; cost allowability, procurement, financial conflict of interest, research security, export controls, human subject protections, research compliance requirements, or other applicable experience which involves evaluating controls over business processes, the efficiency and effectiveness of operations, and compliance with policies/regulations/laws. Experience developing project plans to achieve risk-based project objectives in a complex environment. Professional certifications required, such as CPA, CIA, CISA, CFE, etc. for Senior Auditor role and preferred for Staff Auditor role.

Additional required qualifications include:

  • Knowledge of current internal audit philosophy and practices, including knowledge of internal control testing techniques
  • Uniform Guidance and federal grants management requirements
  • Skill in preparing clear and concise workpapers and comprehensive reports, interpreting and applying policies and regulations, and conducting interviews
  • Sponsored-project administration and subrecipient monitoring
  • Ability to organize work; to conceptualize and prioritize objectives; to evaluate evidence; and to exercise independent judgment based on University of Tennessee policies and regulations
  • Effort reporting, cost allowability, and cost allocation
  • Ability to coach, motivate, and provide performance feedback to team members
  • Procurement in a grant-funded environment
  • Knowledge and awareness of necessity to maintain confidentiality and objectivity
  • Financial conflict of interest (FCOI) requirements
  • Ability to maintain a sense of urgency in approaching internal audit responsibilities
  • Research security and export controls (ITAR/EAR)
  • Competence in Microsoft Office Word and Excel and ability to use other audit software;
  • Human subjects protections (IRB) and animal care/use (IACUC)
  • Ability to handle multiple ongoing projects and independently establish priorities to meet deadlines
  • Research integrity, misconduct processes, and responsible conduct of research (RCR)
  • Ability to exercise independent and mature professional judgment when evaluating audit evidence and formulating recommendations
  • Internal audit methodology, risk assessment, and control evaluation
  • Ability and willingness to travel
  • Data analysis/analytics tools applied to audit testing
  • Strong written and verbal communication, including presenting to senior leadership

Preferred qualifications:

Master's degree

Additional preferred qualifications include:

  • Ability to determine team priorities and allocate time and resources effectively.
  • Knowledge of administrative operations of a higher education institution.
  • Competency in data analysis software. Familiarity with rules and regulations involving externally sponsored research.
  • Supervisory and project management experience.
  • Experience leading audit teams, reviewing work papers, and managing multiple ongoing projects.
  • Experience in an internal audit or research focused function. Experience with data analytics tools.
  • Experience auditing in higher education, research administration, or working in an administrative role in higher education.

Application Process
For full consideration, applications should be accompanied by a letter of interest, a resume, and three professional references. Review of applications will begin immediately.

Benefits and Compensation
Compensation for the position is budgeted for $55,000 - $70,000 for Staff Research Auditor and a salary range of $70,000 - $85,000 for Senior Research Auditor, depending on experience, knowledge and skills of selected candidate.

title: Governance Executive - Macquarie Group
description:
Join our Legal and Governance team in London and contribute to the corporate governance arrangements supporting our businesses across EMEA and Americas. You will become part of a collaborative regional function, working closely with colleagues across Legal, Finance, Tax, Treasury, Risk Management and the wider business groups. Supporting a diverse portfolio of legal entities whilst working with boards, committees, corporate transactions and regulatory developments.

We are a global financial services group operating in 30 markets with 57 years of unbroken profitability. At Macquarie, you're empowered to shape a career that is fulfilling and creates value. What role will you play?

You will provide corporate governance and company secretarial support to a portfolio of entities, primarily across EMEA. Acting as a day-to-day governance support across Macquarie, you will help boards, committees, directors and internal stakeholders navigate governance requirements effectively. This will include preparing for board and committee meetings, drafting standard resolutions, reviewing and preparing papers, taking minutes and tracking actions. You will also coordinate meeting logistics and formalities, including compiling and distributing materials through Diligent Board Books.

Beyond the meeting cycle, you will support corporate transactions such as restructures, dividends, incorporations and dissolutions. Coordinating governance compliance activities, maintaining accurate corporate records and entity data, and preparing relevant documentation to company registrars. You will monitor corporate governance and regulatory developments, consider their implications and translate them into clear actions for the business. There will also be opportunities to enhance governance processes through data, technology and automation, while maintaining appropriate risk and control standards.

  • 3 years' + company secretarial or corporate governance experience, supporting entities across EMEA. With a UK Chartered Governance Institute qualification or progress towards one.

  • Sound judgement and a practical approach to complex governance matters.
  • Ability to take ownership, prioritise and deliver accurately in a fast-paced environment.
  • A continuous improvement mindset and interest in data, technology, automation and AI.

title: Engineer I&C
description:

## Engineer I&C

General Atomics

San Diego

California

Job Summary

General Atomics (GA), and its affiliated companies, is one of the world’s leading resources for high-technology systems development ranging from the nuclear fuel cycle to remotely piloted aircraft, airborne sensors, and advanced electric, electronic, wireless and laser technologies.

The DIII-D National Fusion Facility is the flagship for fusion research in the United States, serving as one of the most flexible and well diagnosed facilities in the world for conducting critical plasma science and technology research that closes gaps on fusion energy. We currently have an exciting opportunity for an Instrumentation and Control (I & C) engineer to work within our Operations Group in support of the DIII-D program in San Diego, CA. This position will apply innovative approaches in deploying, designing and upgrading, the instrumentation and controls associated with the DIII-D tokomak and ancillary systems.

Under direct supervision, the I & C Engineer shall be responsible for overseeing the design, installation, maintenance, and optimization of the I & C systems across plant operations.  This role ensures reliable automation, process control, and compliance with safety and regulatory standards.

**No Visa Sponsorships available for this role.**

**DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES**

- Comply with facility safety standards including, but not limited to, lockout tag out (LOTO) and confined space entry requirements.
- Manage plant instrumentation for Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs),  Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) systems, industrial electronics, and various other, control systems.
- Deploy, troubleshoot and/or repair sensors, data acquisition (DAQ) devices and signal conditioning systems.
- Under the guidance of senior engineers, aid in improving SCADA system reliability, process efficiency, and automation performance.
- Support scientists and senior engineers in collecting and interpreting experimental data.
- Perform laboratory experiments using typical electrical engineering equipment such as multi-meters, oscilloscopes, function/arbitrary waveform generators, logic analyzers, spectrum analyzers, and/or solid state and analog power supplies.
- Design new analog and digital circuits or modify existing circuits to meet specific program requirements.
- Read and interpret electrical and electronic schematic diagrams.
- Update analog and/or digital printed circuit board (PCB) designs containing obsolete components by selecting and substituting suitable replacement components.
- Test and troubleshoot analog and/or digital PCBs and systems
- Update PCB designs to accommodate new components and/or improved functionality.
- Coordinate the fabrication and assembly of PCBs using in-house resources and/or outside vendors
- Test, troubleshoot, repair and/or upgrade industrial electronic systems including relay banks, interlocks, crash button chains, and voice and/or lighting notification systems.

title: Credentialing Specialist
description:
Credentialing Specialist | Full-Time | Remote

Join Our Team at H2 Health!

H2 Health is seeking a detail-oriented and highly organized Credentialing Specialist to join our team in a full-time, remote position!

In this role, you will support our growing healthcare organization by coordinating provider credentialing, insurance payer enrollments, and recredentialing processes. You'll help ensure our physical, occupational, and speech therapy providers maintain accurate and up-to-date credentials so they can continue delivering exceptional patient care.

We're looking for someone who thrives in a detail-driven environment, takes initiative, and enjoys collaborating with clinicians and internal teams.

Responsibilities

  • Coordinate provider and facility credentialing, recredentialing, and enrollment processes with insurance payers, including Medicare, Medicaid, and commercial insurance plans.
  • Review credentialing information available through Medallion, verifying provider details, credentialing status, and supporting documentation for accuracy and completeness.
  • Maintain and update provider profiles in the Council for Affordable Quality Healthcare (CAQH) system, including required attestations and supporting documentation.
  • Assist clinicians with National Provider Identifier (NPI) applications and updates.
  • Monitor professional licenses, certifications, expiration dates, and other required credentialing documentation.
  • Ensure newly hired providers are added to applicable insurance payer rosters and terminated providers are removed as required.
  • Track credentialing applications, renewals, outstanding documentation, and payer enrollment status to support timely completion.
  • Communicate with clinicians, insurance representatives, and internal departments to obtain information and resolve credentialing discrepancies.
  • Assist clinicians with fingerprinting and other documentation required for credentialing.
  • Maintain confidential, accurate, and organized credentialing records in accordance with applicable regulations and company policies.
  • Support additional administrative and compliance-related tasks as needed.

Requirements

  • High school diploma or equivalent preferred.
  • Previous experience in medical office administration, healthcare credentialing, provider enrollment, or a related healthcare administrative role preferred.
  • Familiarity with CAQH, NPI applications, insurance credentialing, and payer enrollment processes preferred.
  • Ability to review and interpret provider credentialing records in electronic platforms, including Medallion or similar systems.
  • Strong attention to detail, organizational skills, and ability to manage multiple deadlines.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications and electronic recordkeeping.
  • Ability to work independently in a remote setting while maintaining strong communication and accountability.
  • Commitment to protecting confidential provider and patient information.

Benefits

At H2 Health, we value our team members and are committed to supporting their professional and personal well-being.

As a full-time employee, you'll have access to:

  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance
  • Paid time off (PTO) and paid holidays
  • 401(k) retirement plan
  • Professional development and growth opportunities
  • A collaborative and supportive team environment
  • Full-time remote work

Why H2 Health?

At H2 Health, our mission is to make a meaningful difference in the lives of the patients and communities we serve. Behind every great clinician is a dedicated team working to ensure they have the support they need to succeed.

We foster a culture of collaboration, accountability, and continuous improvement, where every team member plays an important role in our success.

Ready to Join Our Team?

If you're organized, detail-oriented, and passionate about supporting healthcare professionals, we'd love to hear from you!

Apply today and Dare to Make a Difference with H2 Health!

H2 Health is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to any legally protected status.

title: Operator III (Machine Shop)
description:
Eaton’s EPG CHD EP Americas division is currently seeking a Operator III (Machine Shop).

The hourly rate for this position is $21.90 per hour.

Please note the salary information shown above is a general guideline only. Salaries are based upon candidate skills, experience, and qualifications, as well as market and business considerations.

What you’ll do:

PRIMARY FUNCTION:
This position is responsible for setting up and operating conventional, special-purpose, and numerical control (NC) machines and machining centers to fabricate metallic and non-metallic parts. The incumbent will also fit and assemble machine parts into complete units, applying knowledge of machine shop theory and procedures, shop mathematics, machinability of materials, and layout techniques.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:
1. Studies blueprints, sketches, drawings, manuals, specifications, and sample parts to determine dimensions and tolerances of finished workpiece, sequence of operations, or setup requirements
2. Measures, marks, and scribes dimensions and reference points on material or workpiece as guides for subsequent machining
3. Selects, aligns, and secures holding fixtures, cutting tools, attachments, accessories, and materials on machines; such as mills, lathes, jig borers, grinders, and shapers
4. Calculates and sets controls to regulate machining factors such as speed, feed, coolant flow, and dept and angle of cut; or enters commands to retrieve, input, or edit computerized machine control media
5. Starts and observes machine operations to detect malfunctions and out-of-tolerance machining, and adjusts machine controls or control media as required
6. Verifies conformance of finished workpiece to specifications, using precision measuring instruments
7. Sets up and operates machine on trial run to verify accuracy of machine settings or programmed control data
8. Fits and assembles parts into complete assembly using jigs, fixtures, surface plate, surface table, hand tools, and power tools
9. Verifies dimensions and alignment of assembly, using measuring instruments such as micrometers, height gauges, and gauge blocks
10. May develop specifications from general description and draw sketch of part or product to be fabricated
11. May confer with engineers, production personnel, programmers, or others to resolve machining or assembly problems
12. Performs other duties as assigned

Qualifications:

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:
1. Must be legally authorized to work in the US without company sponsorship
2. Must have a high school diploma or GED from an accredited institution
3. Understanding of basic CNC control functions, machining, and basic math functions
4. Minimum of 2 years experience in a multiple process-manufacturing environment
5. Knowledge of various measuring instruments and ability to read blueprints.
6. This position requires use of information or access to hardware which is subject to the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR). All applications must be US persons within the meaning of ITAR. ITAR defines a US person as a US Citizen, US Permanent Resident (i.e. “Green Card Holder”), Political Asylee, or Refugee
7. Remain standing for an extended period of time up to 8 hours
8. Able to lift to 35 lbs. on a regular basis

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

1. Two years of work experience in a machine shop

Role Title: Cloud Platform Security Architect

Role purpose / summary

Job Description:

The Cloud Platform & Security Architect is responsible for defining and governing the architecture of FSCS cloud, hybrid infrastructure and security platforms. The role provides strategic and technical architectural leadership across Microsoft Azure, cloud platforms, networking, identity, security and resilience, ensuring technology solutions are secure, scalable, resilient, supportable and aligned with FSCS technology strategy and architectural principles.

The role defines target-state architectures, reference architectures, technical standards, patterns and architectural guardrails that guide the design and evolution of FSCS technology platforms.

Working closely with Enterprise Architecture, Information and Cyber Security, the IT Infrastructure & Security Manager, Product and Engineering teams, and strategic technology partners, the role provides architecture direction and design assurance across technology change and investment.

The role acts as a senior technical authority for cloud platform and security architecture, supporting strategic technology decisions while ensuring solutions remain aligned with FSCS business, security, resilience and operational requirements.

My Priorities - what I will deliver

Cloud Platform Architecture

  • Define and maintain target-state architecture for Microsoft Azure, cloud and hybrid technology platforms.
  • Define reference architectures and reusable patterns for Azure landing zones, Management Groups, subscriptions, networking, identity, compute, storage, monitoring and governance.
  • Establish architectural principles and guardrails covering Azure Policy, RBAC, PIM, private connectivity, resource organisation, logging and platform governance.
  • Define architecture patterns that enable scalable, secure and consistent technology delivery across FSCS.
  • Provide architectural direction for cloud migration, modernisation and re-platforming initiatives.
  • Assess new Azure services and cloud technologies and provide recommendations for their adoption.
  • Ensure cloud architecture balances security, resilience, scalability, performance, operational supportability and cost efficiency.
  • Define architectural direction for Infrastructure as Code and automated cloud provisioning, including Terraform and Azure DevOps.
  • Maintain cloud platform architecture roadmaps aligned with FSCS technology strategy.

Hybrid Infrastructure Architecture

  • Define target-state architecture for FSCS hybrid infrastructure and its integration with Microsoft Azure.
  • Define target-state architectural patterns and standards for core infrastructure services, including technologies such as Active Directory, Entra ID, DNS, DHCP and PKI.
  • Provide architectural direction for compute, virtualisation, storage and associated platform technologies.
  • Define secure and resilient integration patterns between cloud, on-premises and third-party environments.
  • Develop architecture roadmaps supporting infrastructure modernisation and reduction of legacy technology.
  • Identify architectural dependencies, constraints and technical debt associated with hybrid infrastructure.
  • Ensure infrastructure architecture supports agreed security, resilience, lifecycle and operational requirements.

Network & Connectivity Architecture

  • Define target-state network architecture across cloud and hybrid environments.
  • Define reference architectures and patterns for Azure networking, routing, segmentation, firewalls, private connectivity, VPN, load balancing and application delivery.
  • Define network architecture aligned with FSCS Zero Trust principles and security requirements.
  • Provide architectural direction across Azure networking, Cisco technologies, Zscaler and associated network and security platforms.
  • Define secure connectivity patterns between Azure, on-premises infrastructure, SaaS services, third parties and external services.
  • Establish architecture standards and principles for network resilience, segmentation, availability and secure connectivity.
  • Assess emerging networking technologies and recommend appropriate strategic direction.

Security Architecture & Technical Controls

  • Define cloud platform and infrastructure security architecture aligned with FSCS security policies, enterprise architecture principles and regulatory requirements.
  • Define security architecture patterns and technical guardrails across cloud, identity, network and infrastructure platforms.
  • Provide architectural direction for Microsoft Defender, Sentinel and associated Microsoft security technologies.
  • Define identity architecture covering Entra ID, Conditional Access, PIM, RBAC, MFA, SSO, managed identities and workload identities.
  • Define architectural patterns for Azure Firewall, WAF, DDoS Protection, Key Vault, encryption, certificates and secrets management.
  • Define architecture patterns aligned with Zero Trust principles across identity, networks, applications and cloud platforms.
  • Ensure security, vulnerability management, hardening, logging and monitoring requirements are incorporated into reference architectures and solution designs.
  • Work closely with Information and Cyber Security to ensure platform architectures align with security policies, standards and risk requirements.
  • Evaluate emerging security technologies and recommend appropriate architectural approaches.

Resilience, Backup & Disaster Recovery

  • Define architecture principles and patterns for availability, resilience, backup, recovery and disaster recovery.
  • Define appropriate resilience and redundancy patterns for critical cloud and hybrid platforms.
  • Ensure architecture supports agreed recovery objectives and operational resilience requirements.
  • Define reference architectures for backup, replication, failover and recovery capabilities.
